```text
Habeas traces a project's requirements, written in its mdBook, to the source
code and tests that implement and verify them.

- A requirement is a {req} directive in the book that states obligations with
  MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY. A named example is an {example} directive
  describing a concrete case of one or more requirements. Both have
  dot-separated full names, such as requirements.cli.status. A vocabulary
  definition, a {definition} directive, defines a term that other text uses with
  {term}; it is never the target of a reference.
- Source code marks the requirements and examples it implements, tests, or
  relies on with {impl}, {test}, and {cite} references, such as
  {impl}`requirements.cli.status`, and acknowledges known gaps in them with
  {fixme} references.
- Sources are identified by outline nodes: a file's functions, types, sections,
  and similar items, named by selectors such as fn[run] or impl[Thing]/fn[run].
  <root> is the whole file.
```

```text
The reference roles:

- {impl}: the source implements part of the requirement or example. Source code
  implements part of one when it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an
  output, or handles a case it specifies, or when it constrains a type's fields,
  variants, serialized form, or validation. Calling code that implements it, or
  producing a value a caller uses to meet it, does not by itself count. A check
  counts only if the text states it, or the item could not meet one of the
  text's obligations without it; then returning its outcome counts even when a
  caller acts on it. Code that checks it is consistent with a requirement, such
  as recognizing a form the requirement defines in order to decide whether to
  run other behavior, relies on that requirement ({cite}) rather than
  implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a
  kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the code that carries
  out the convention as a whole, not by each item that produces one such output.
  A source root demonstrating a stated structural obligation should carry
  {impl}. Authors may add the marker up front or on a structural reviewer’s recommendation. Tests supply evidence for
  behavioral obligations. Only a root needs the reference: an item that no other item marked {impl}
  for the same requirement reaches. Code a reviewer reaches by following a
  marked item, through what it calls, the types it uses, or the implementations
  of trait methods it calls, needs none; nor does a test helper reached from a
  test marked {test}. A site of a
  distributed requirement needs no reference to it for being a site.
- {test}: the source is a test or test helper designed to verify behavior the
  requirement or example specifies.
- {cite}: the source relies on or refers to the requirement or example, and
  should be re-checked or kept in sync when it changes, without implementing or
  testing it. A {cite} needs no coverage; each item with citations has its own
  citation review.
- {fixme}: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the requirement or
  example. It is always fenced; its body describes the gap and may begin with
  lines such as :github: rust-lang/rust#123 naming issues that track it.

A declaration can also name a whole file or one outline node it is implemented
or tested by, with an :impl: or :test: option line directly after its opening
fence; that counts as an {impl} or {test} reference from that source. A
reference written as a fence, :::{role} name, then commentary, then :::,
attaches commentary.
```

```text
A distributed requirement states obligations that each of many sites upholds on
its own. It contains site queries, which select its sites, and violation
queries, which select constructs likely to break those obligations. Each site is
the innermost outline node containing a site-query match.
```
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.habeas_background` states only observable prompt content. Every assessment prompt MUST replace `{{habeas_background}}` with the first text. Requirement, example and citation prompts MUST replace `{{reference_roles}}` with the second text. The site prompt and distributed task MUST replace `{{distributed_background}}` with the third text.

The clauses name no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that the implementation must use or delegate to. Each clause could be met by a different construction with the same rendered prompts. Examples are a template engine, string substitution, or texts embedded at build time or read at run time. All of these produce identical prompts, so how the replacement is built is discretionary. No clause creates a structural obligation, so no implementation root is needed. The review roots are empty and there are no acknowledgments. Whether the rendered prompts contain the right texts is a behavioral matter for the test-adequacy criterion.

behavioral: The tests cover all three substitutions in `requirements.authoring.habeas_background`. They compare against the requirement's own text blocks. The helpers `approved_text` and `distributed_background` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` read the blocks from `md/requirements/authoring.md`, so the expected text is not taken from the implementation.

**Obligation 1: every assessment prompt replaces `{{habeas_background}}` with the first text.**
- `mod[tests]/fn[subjects_of_one_kind_share_a_byte_identical_system_prompt]` builds prompts for structural, example, citation and site subjects. It asserts that each system prompt contains `approved_text("habeas_background", 0)`.
- `fn[initial_prompt_carries_the_review_criteria]` checks the requirement and example prompts for the same block and asserts that no `{{` remains.
- `fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` checks the serialized citation request.
- `fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` checks the site request.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` asserts exact equality of the whole system prompt with the template after substituting the first block, for both a requirement and an example.

**Obligation 2: requirement, example and citation prompts replace `{{reference_roles}}` with the second text.**
- The shared-prompt test asserts the second block is present for every template except `site_prompt`. That covers structural, requirement/example, and citation prompts.
- It also asserts the block is absent from the site prompt.
- The criteria test and the citation test assert the block directly.
- The CLI test asserts the exact system prompt for a requirement and an example.
- The site test asserts the block is absent from the site prompt.

**Obligation 3: the site prompt and distributed task replace `{{distributed_background}}` with the third text.**
- The site test asserts the site request contains `distributed_background()`.
- It also compares `initial.subject` to the filled `site_prompt` template.
- `fn[a_distributed_requirement_task_continues_with_the_filled_distributed_task]` fills `distributed_task` with the third text. It asserts the task starts with that text and that the subject message of a distributed requirement contains the task.
- It also asserts that the task is absent from the system prompt, and that the prompt contains no `{{`.
- `fn[initial_prompt_carries_the_review_criteria]` asserts that a non-distributed requirement's prompt does not contain the third text.

I found no uncovered obligation or boundary.
